item.title: Utah couple built a $2 million backyard pool with a 90-foot mountain and a scuba-diving tunnel
item.description: In Utah, a dedicated couple has poured $2 million into an extraordinary backyard pool designed specifically for scuba diving. This stunning installation boasts a remarkable 90-foot artificial mountain, five magnificent waterfalls, and an exhilarating underwater tunnel. By creating such a bespoke sanctuary, they provide a fantastic recreational escapade for scuba lovers, complete with a lazy river and a fully equipped kitchen set within the mountain's embrace.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Florida commits $8.7 million to preserve two working ranches
item.description: Florida has enacted a permanent conservation measure for two significant ranches located in Manatee and Highlands counties, encompassing nearly 1,500 acres. This initiative is designed to safeguard local agricultural practices and boost the economy. Through the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, the state aims to uphold agricultural land under conservation, as stressed by Commissioner Wilton Simpson for forthcoming generations, highlighting Florida's intent to preserve its agricultural legacy sustainably.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Demi Moore’s Idaho home has a river, mountain views and wild elk in her backyard
item.description: Demi Moore has chosen to settle in Hailey, Idaho, immersed in the enchanting landscape of Sun Valley. She revels in the outdoor experiences available at her riverside retreat, including swimming, kayaking, and fly-fishing throughout the summer months. Initially intended as a vacation haven, the property has become her permanent residence. The area seamlessly marries rustic allure with an artistic vibe, drawing in art lovers for gallery excursions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: 5-year-old asks for a baseball field, Ohio dad spends $30,000 building one in backyard
item.description: An Ohio father spent nearly two years and around $30,000 building a baseball field in his backyard after his five-year-old son requested one. Jason Kidd transformed his property into a playing field with professional-grade clay, regulation bases and a raised pitcher's mound. Despite complaints from neighbours and unfinished additions, Kidd said the project was about spending time with his son and teaching him baseball.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mother left two sons out of her will after family dispute; New Jersey court sides with daughters
item.description: A New Jersey mother who initially planned to divide her estate equally among her four children changed her will in 2016, excluding both sons after their relationship deteriorated. Following her death in 2024, the sons challenged the decision, alleging that their sisters had influenced her. One daughter had been her sole caregiver since 1996. However, on October 16, 2026, a New Jersey appeals court upheld the revised will.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Side Hustle Grows Steadily: $500 yard games fund Little Party Co.; she keeps corporate job
item.description: Vanessa Romano launched Little Party Co. with just a $500 investment in outdoor party games, inspired by social media trends. Within a few months, her savvy approach catapulted her revenue to over $9,000. She strategically reinvested her profits while balancing a full-time corporate career and family. Rather than abandoning her corporate job, Romano embraces both roles, demonstrating that entrepreneurship can flourish without choosing between them.

item.title: California farm earns 10 times more leasing land for solar than growing wheat
item.description: In Tulare County, California, the Changala family farm has embraced a transformative shift from dry-farmed wheat to solar energy. Driven by financial incentives, solar leases are now yielding significantly greater income compared to traditional crops. Facing water scarcity in the San Joaquin Valley, farmers are increasingly investing in solar technologies.

item.title: In 1968, Cassandra Henderson graduated from a North Carolina school; 58 years later, she returned to its restored building, now 53 senior apartments
item.description: After years away, Cassandra Henderson has made her way back to Yanceyville, North Carolina, settling into the revitalized Dillard School Apartments. Originally a school from 1949 until 2002, this historical building has now been transformed into 53 affordable housing units for seniors, tackling the local housing crisis. This renovation not only honors the past but also strengthens community ties by providing necessary living spaces.

Cost-of-living protests: Italian police clash with protesters in Milan, Bologna
item.description: Protests against inflation, low wages, and public service issues turned violent in multiple Italian cities. In Milan, protests erupted in Piazza Duomo where demonstrators clashed with police and vandalized property. Bologna saw similar unrest, with hooded youths attacking the central railway station and throwing projectiles at security forces. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence while supporting peaceful demonstrations.
item.dc:creator: Ayush Pandey

item.title: San Diego weighs $4.2B project with 4,254 homes and $460M in public upgrades
item.description: San Diego is pushing forward with an ambitious redevelopment project for 48.5 acres surrounding Pechanga Arena. This initiative aims to introduce 4,254 housing units, a significant number of which will be affordable. In addition to a new 16,000-seat arena, the plan includes approximately $460 million in upgrades to local infrastructure. The goal is to foster a more walkable community with improved public spaces.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia executes five nationals on terrorism charges, death toll hits 188
item.description: Five men were executed in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province for terrorism-related charges after their convictions were upheld. The total number of executions in the kingdom has now reached 188 this year, marking a significant increase. According to the Ministry of Interior, these men were convicted of serious crimes against security personnel and were affiliated with a foreign terrorist organization.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: In 2016, Muhammad Ali’s former training camp was bought for $520,000; in 2019 it opened as Fighter’s Heaven
item.description: Mike Madden's dedication to preserving sports history shines brightly as he invests $1.5 million into restoring Fighter's Heaven, the legendary training camp originally founded by Muhammad Ali in 1972. After years of neglect, the camp reopened to an enthusiastic public in June 2019, earning praise from Pennsylvania’s State Historic Preservation Office for its cultural importance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rare gold LEGO mask found in donated jewellery bag sold for $18,101
item.description: A small gold LEGO mask found inside a donated jewellery bag at a Goodwill store in Pennsylvania turned out to be a rare collector's item. Initially listed for $14.95, the 14-karat gold Bionicle Kanohi Hau mask attracted bids from collectors and eventually sold for $18,101 in March 2024. Only 30 such masks were produced in 2001.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Martha’s Vineyard rejects 54-acre housing plan after seven marathon meetings
item.description: Martha's Vineyard's planning board has turned down the Katama Meadows housing initiative after thorough discussions. This project sought to meet housing demands through a mix of affordable and market-rate homes catering to essential workers. However, environmental concerns regarding nitrogen pollution and the inclusion of luxury properties raised significant opposition, leading to the decision. The land remains with the developers, who may consider a revised proposal in the future.
